Briefly stated the present case was registered on the complaint of complainant Saifullah Ansari,
who mentioned in his complaint that he (complainant) came to know about accused Nabi Alam Ray,
who was working as an agent facilitating overseas employment.

In December 2023, the complainant contacted the accused on his mobile phone and during conversation, the accused offered the complainant a job of Data Entry Operator in Cambodia assuring him a monthly income of 700-800 USD with food and accommodation.

After reaching an agreement, complainant paid Rs.20,000/- in cash to mother of the accused in late December 2023 and on 13.01.2024, additional amount of Rs.30,000/- was transferred to the account number provided by the accused via Phonepe.

On 15.01.2024, complainant handed over Rs.50,000/- in cash to accused at his (accused) rented house near Kapashera Border, Delhi, and on the same day, he (complainant) boarded a flight from Delhi to Bangkok.

Upon landing at Bangkok, a driver met the complainant at the airport and drove the complainant directly to Combodia-Thailand border, where associates of accused namely Pathan and Kalam took passport of complainant.

Complainant reached capital of Cambodia, where in a hotel,
Pathan and Kalam met him (complainant) and informed the complainant that complainant would be working for a Chinese company involved Judgment 2 of 11 FIR NO. 255/2024 State Vs. Nabi Alam Ray in scams targeting Indian nationals.

Despite protests of complainant, Pathan and Kalam threatened the complainant, insisting that he (complainant) comply with whatever job they (Pathan and Kalam) assigned if he (complainant) wanted his passport back.
After that complainant started working for the company, where complainant was mentally tortured by threatening fines on his monthly salary for minor infractions.
The complainant endured verbal abused and faced physical threats, he made any mistakes during the scripted interactions.
Somehow, the complainant managed to escape from the clutches of accused persons Pathan and Kalam and on 10.05.2024, the complainant returned to India.
3. On the aforesaid complaint, present FIR was got registered under section 370/420/34 IPC.
4. During investigations of the case, statement of witnesses were recorded.

On the basis of investigation, the accused persons were charge-sheeted for offence punishable under Section 370/420/34 IPC.
5.

During the trial of the case, accused Nabi Alam Ray was tried vide order dated 04.04.2025 on the following charge:-
"......That in the month of December 2023 and on 15.01.2024, at unknown time, at your rented house at Kapashera, within the jurisdiction of PS Kapashera, you by deceiving the complainant on the pretext of providing a job of Data Entry Operator in a company situated at Cambodia, cheated an amount of Rs. 70,000/- and thereby you committed an offence punishable u/s 420 IPC within the cognizance of this Judgment 3 of 11 FIR NO. 255/2024 State Vs. Nabi Alam Ray court.

Secondly, on 15.01.2024, at unknown time, the complainant was taken to Bangkok by flight and from Bangkok to Cambodia by road, where you in criminal conspiracy with other accused persons namely Pathan and Kalam (since not arrested) had forced the complainant to hand over his passport and other accused persons namely Pathan and State vs Nabi Alam Ray on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65150120/
2 Kalam (since not arrested) had taken the passport of the complainant so that he cannot leave Cambodia and be forced to work in a Chainies scam company targeting Indian public for scam/cheating and thereby you committed an offence punishable u/s 370 r/w/s 120B and 34 IPC within cognizance of this court......."
6. Accused Nabi Alam Ray pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
7.
To prove its case, prosecution examined two witnesses.
PW-1 complainant Saifullah Ansari deposed that he has studied upto 10th class and is a meson by profession.
He contacted one Azhar as he wished to go to foreign country for work.
Azhar asked him to talk to accused Nabi Alam, who told him that he (accused) can make arrangement to send him (PW-1) to Cambodia for Data Operating work.
Accused further assured him a salary of Rs.70,000/- per month for that work.
Azhar made arrangement for his visit to Cambodia.
He paid Rs. One lac to the accused.
He further stated that he took a flight from Delhi to Bangkok and from Bangkok, he went to Cambodia by road.

At Cambodia,
2 persons namely Kalam and Pathan met him at Cambodia.
Azhar had already told him that Pathan and Kalam would meet him at Cambodia.
He was employed in a Chainies company, where he was compelled to do cleaning work.
He was not given Data Operating work.
He contacted Azhar and Judgment 4 of 11 FIR NO. 255/2024 State Vs. Nabi Alam Ray informed him that he (PW-1) had not been given the data operating work.
Azhar was angry on him.
Azhar did not make any arrangement to bring him back.
His passport was taken by the company and same was not given to him back despite his repeated requests.
Then he somehow fled away from the company and reached to Indian Embassy and with the help of Embassy, he came back to India.
He made a complaint via e-mail to police, on the basis of which FIR No. 255/24 Ex PW 1/A was registered.
He tried to contact number of times to Azhar for his money, which he had given to the accused.
Azhar did not pick up his phone.
He even contacted the accused and asked him to give back his (PW-1) money.
Now, the accused had returned his money.
Accused is residing in his neighbour.
His visa was arranged by Azhar.
He was sent on tourist visa and was told by Azhar that company would make further arrangement of his visa.
PW-1 further deposed that during investigation, police also got recorded his statement before Magistrate.
PW-1 proved statement recorded u/s 164 CrPC as Ex.PW1/B.
This witness has been cross-examined by Ld. defence counsel.
After cross-examination of PW-1, he was declared hostile by Ld. Addl. P.P during the cross-examination and was cross-examined by Ld. Addl. P.P for State.

During cross-examination by Ld. Addl. P.P for State, PW-1 admitted that he named the accused in his examination in chief as the person, who had taken money of Rs. One lac from him for making arrangement.
However, he denied the other suggestions put to him on behalf of State.
8. PW-2 Inspector Vijay deposed that on 26.05.2024, he Judgment 5 of 11 FIR NO. 255/2024 State Vs. Nabi Alam Ray was posted at PS Kapashera.

On that day, one mail was received from NIA, on the official mail ID of the SHO, PS Kapashera, alleging therein accused Nabi Alam Ray alongwith his associates has dishonestly taken money from complainant on the pretext of sending him to foreign country for some office work and instead sent him to South Asian Countries Combodia wherein some chinese call centre was operated who used to dupe people on the pretext of acting as various civic agency as CBI, NIA, Police and anothers and thus, accordingly, the case FIR No. 255/24 u/s 370/420/34 IPC Ex.PW1/A was registered and investigation was taken up.
PW-2 further stated that during course of investigation, accused Nabi Alam Ray was arrested vide memo Ex.PX5.

Various documents and three passports were seized from accused and search for other co-accused persons were made, all were found to be residing out of India.
White passport visa of complainant Ex. PX7 (colly) was sent for verification which is pending yet to be verified from concerned consulate / embassy.
Money sent to accused Nabi Alam Ray via phone-pay is proved as Ex.PX-1D.

Account opening form Ex.PX-12 and also got verified

Money sent to accused via pay-tm in his SBI Account were also verified vide Ex.PX-18 (colly).
Statement of Judgment 6 of 11 FIR NO. 255/2024 State Vs. Nabi Alam Ray complainant u/s 164 Cr.P.C. were got recorded from Ld. Duty MM vide Ex.PX-20 (colly).
Statement of SI Utkarsh Bansal from AHTD/ NIA HQ were also got recorded u/s 161 Cr.P.C. and annexed with the case file.
Statement of Insp. R.K. Meena, AHTD/NIA HQ were also got recorded u/s 161 Cr.P.C. and annexed with the case file.

He recorded the statements of other witnesses during investigation alongwith supplementary statement of the complainant and after approval of the senior official, the same was charge-sheeted before the Hon'ble Court.
This witness has been cross-examined by accused.

9. In his statement recorded u/s 294 CrPC, accused Nabi Alam Ray admitted certificate u/s 65B of Indian Evidence Act regarding FIR as Ex.PX-1, certificate u/s 65B of Indian Evidence Act regarding e-mail as Ex.PX-2, seizure memo of 2 mobile phones and 2 pen drives as Ex.PX-3, seizure memo of passport and documents as Ex.PX-4, arrest memo of accused as Ex.PX-5, personal search memo of accused as Ex.PX-6, photocopy of passport of complainant as Ex.PX-7 (colly), photocopy of application form for EC of complainant as Ex.PX-8, photocopy of statement by returnee scamming company victims of India at Cambodia as Ex.PX-9, photocopy of transaction to accused by the complainant as Ex.PX-10, photocopy of bank statement of accused as Ex.PX-11 (colly), photocopy of account opening form of accused as Ex.PX-12 (colly), photocopy of visa of complainant as Ex.PX-13,
photocopy of ticket of complainant as Ex.PX-14 (colly), reply of Spicejet Nodal Officer u/s 91 CrPC as Ex.PX-15, notice u/s 91 CrPC to Air Asia Ltd. as Ex.PX-16, Notice to Deputy Secretary, MEA,
regarding verification of visa of complainant as Ex.PX-17, Judgment 7 of 11 FIR NO. 255/2024 State Vs. Nabi Alam Ray certificate u/s 65B of Indian Evidence Act given by PayTM and other documents as Ex.PX-18 (colly), Notice u/s 91 CrPC to PayTM as Ex.PX-19, complete proceedings u/s 164 CrPC as Ex.PX-20 (colly), photocopy of reply given by MEA dated 22.07.2024 as Ex.PX-21 (colly), reply of notice u/s 91 CrPC and supporting documents by Air Asia as Ex.PX-22 (colly).
10. Since all prosecution witnesses were examined / dropped by the prosecution, prosecution evidence was closed.
11. Since no incriminating evidence had emerged, the statement of the accused persons under Section 313 Cr. PC was dispensed with.
12. I have heard State through Sh. V.K. Swami, Ld. Additional PP for State and Ld. counsel for accused.
I have also perused entire material on record.

4 13.
The prosecution witness has apparently not supported the foundation of the FIR.
The complainant (PW-1) has deposed during his cross-examination that the accused has not much to do in the offence.

To further exonerate the accused, PW-1/Complainant has specifically stated that it was one person with the name Azhar (not accused in the present case) who assured him for providing a job of Data Entry Operator and asked him to arrange money for the same.
The relevant portion of his cross-examination is as under:-
".......It is correct that the accused present in the Court today has not much to do in the offence.

It was Azhar, Judgment 8 of 11 FIR NO. 255/2024 State Vs. Nabi Alam Ray who assured me for providing a job of Data Entry Operator and he asked me to arrange money for the same, which I had given to Azhar in the presence of the accused.
I named accused in my complaint/FIR as accused was with Azhar at the time of taking money by Azhar and I was under the impression that accused had deceived me and took my money.

It is correct that in fact Azhar had deceived me,
took money from my on the pretext of arranging a job of Data Entry Operator for a salary of Rs.70,000/-.

It is correct that I continuously contacted Azhar after coming back to India for returning money but he did not pick up my phone or he once or twice when picked up my phone, told me that call to the accused, therefore, I named the accused in my complaint.
It is correct that accused Nabi Alam had paid my money to me and now, I do not have any grievance against the accused, however, I request the Court to take legal action against Azhar.
Azhar had my life miserable at Cambodia."
14. Even during cross-examination on behalf of State, PW-1 / complainant did not support the case of the prosecution.

Relevant portion of his cross-examination is as under:-
".......It is incorrect to suggest that the accused had deceived.
(Vol. The accused rather returned my money back.)
It is incorrect to suggest that as I have already reached on a settlement and received my money back from the accused, I am deposing falsely to save him from the clutches of law.
It is incorrect to suggest that the accused had made all the arrangements for sending me to Cambodia on the pretext of providing me a job of Data Entry Operator at Cambodia.
It is incorrect to suggest that the accused had cheated me in connivance with Azhar.
(Vol. It was Azhar, who had cheated me and sent me to Cambodia on false ticket for arranging a job of Data Entry Operator.)
It is incorrect to suggest that I am deposing falsely as the accused is my neighbour or that I have been won over or pressurized to make a false statement.
It is incorrect to suggest that I have deposed falsely."

15. The court would observe that the statement of PW-1 is by itself not free from the suspicion of an account retracted for Judgment 9 of 11 FIR NO. 255/2024 State Vs. Nabi Alam Ray unexplained reasons.
It is certainly discernible that he failed to ascribe any role to the accused whom he had named in the FIR.
Yet, any adverse finding against an accused can be based only on an assertive description of the role played by an accused person in the commission of the alleged offence.
PW-1 did not support the charge in such a manner.

State vs Nabi Alam Ray on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65150120/
5 16.

Since the benefit of competing interpretations and doubts in the prosecution version must always accrue to the accused, the failure of PW-1 to incriminate accused Nabi Alam Ray translates into acquittal of accused.
The prosecution has failed to prove the charge on the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt.

17. The burden of proof in a criminal trial never shifts and it is always the burden of prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of acceptable evidence produced before court.
Crime is an event in real life and is the product of interplay of different human emotions.

In arriving at the conclusion about the guilt of accused, charged with the commission of a crime, a criminal court has to ensure that facts constituting such crime are proved beyond the scope of any reasonable doubt.
Every case in the final analysis would have to depend upon its own facts and merits.
Definite doubts or lacunae in the case of the prosecution may result in benefit of doubt being given to the accused and consequential acquittal.
18. In the light of testimony of material witness, which is exonerating accused, it is held that prosecution has failed to establish charge against accused.
Accordingly, accused Nabi Alam Judgment 10 of 11 FIR NO. 255/2024 State Vs. Nabi Alam Ray Ray stands acquitted under Section 420/370 r/w 120B and 34 IPC.
